scenes.headline: The stator stays still.
scenes.detail: Its three-phase winding creates a rotating magnetic field.
scenes.caption: The stator stays still. Its three-phase winding creates a rotating magnetic field.

scenes.headline: Calculate field speed
scenes.detail: nₛ = 120 f ÷ p     f = 50 Hz     p = 4 poles
scenes.caption: Use one hundred and twenty times frequency divided by total pole count.

scenes.headline: 50 Hz, 4 poles → 1,500 r/min
scenes.detail: That is synchronous field speed, not a shaft reading.
scenes.caption: Fifty hertz with four poles gives one thousand five hundred revolutions per minute for the rotating field.

scenes.headline: The rotor runs below field speed
scenes.detail: Slip enables induction and torque. Exact shaft speed is not provided here.
scenes.caption: In motoring operation the rotor runs below synchronous speed. No motor-specific shaft speed is measured or claimed.

claimBoundary: 1500 r/min is the calculated synchronous stator-field speed for 50 Hz and four total poles. It is not a measured or predicted rotor shaft speed.
